raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Part of #43304: router CPU usage is available, but there is no distribution of time spent handling each message. Add the router processing-time item so operators can distinguish costly routing/sends from downstream work.

## Modifications

- Add `sglang:detokenizer_router_processing_seconds`, enabled only by `--enable-metrics` in multi-detokenizer mode.
- Time routing, batch splitting and outgoing sends after `sock_recv` returns. Include blocking/failed sends; exclude receive wait and incoming deserialization.
- Record once per received message, including control broadcasts and empty batches, regardless of fan-out. Disabled metrics create no histogram or clock reads.
- Preserve routing behavior and document metric boundaries and a PromQL example.

This is complementary to #43323 (CPU), #44390 (throughput) and #44524 (worker identity). It covers only router processing time, so it does not close #43304 or add queue-latency/worker-processing metrics.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU-only, Linux x86_64, Python 3.12.14 and PyTorch 2.14.1+cpu; no model/server launch:

- Before implementation, the three new tests fail because the router has no metrics initialization path; the existing 23 manager tests pass.
- After implementation, the full manager module passes: **26 tests** (also run directly with unittest).
- Manager tests plus neighboring metrics-utils and mocked CPU-monitor coverage: **36 passed, 2 subtests passed**.
- Tests use real Prometheus histograms with an isolated registry, controlled receive/send clocks, grouped batch routing, broadcasts, failed sends, disabled instrumentation and launcher flag propagation.
- All applicable `pre-commit run --files` checks pass; `git diff --check` and MDX compilation pass.

Commands:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py \
  test/registered/unit/observability/test_metrics_utils.py \
  test/registered/unit/observability/test_cpu_monitor.py::TestCpuMonitorMocked -q
PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py
pre-commit run --files python/sglang/srt/managers/multi_tokenizer_mixin.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py docs/docs/references/production_metrics.mdx
```

Validation limitations:
- The existing `TestCpuMonitor.test_cpu_monitor` was attempted and fails in this execution container: psutil reports `NoSuchProcess(pid=2)` because the PID namespace and mounted `/proc` disagree. Its production code is unchanged; the mocked CPU-monitor test passes.
- Mintlify 4.2.559 `mint validate` is blocked by `uv_interface_addresses` (container network-interface restriction). The changed page compiles with the installed MDX compiler.
- The full repository suite, GPU inference, serving integration and full Mintlify build have not been validated.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference-speed improvement claimed. Enabled instrumentation adds two clock reads and one histogram observation per received message; no per-request labels are added. Serving overhead has not been benchmarked.

## Checklist

- [x] Changed files pass pre-commit.
- [x] Focused regression coverage added to the existing registered CPU test.
- [x] Metric semantics and query documented.

@@ -7,6 +7,18 @@ SGLang exposes the following metrics via Prometheus. You can enable it by adding
 
 An example of the monitoring dashboard is available in [examples/monitoring/grafana.json](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/examples/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/json/sglang-dashboard.json).
 
+## Detokenizer router processing time
+
+With `--detokenizer-worker-num > 1` and `--enable-metrics`, `sglang:detokenizer_router_processing_seconds` measures the wall-clock time spent routing each received scheduler message. It includes batch splitting, serialization, and sends to detokenizer workers, including blocking sends. It excludes waiting for and deserializing the incoming message, and does not measure inter-process queue latency or detokenizer worker processing time.
+
+Each message produces one observation, including control broadcasts, empty batches, and messages whose handling raises an exception. A batch sent to multiple workers still produces one observation. This is a per-message histogram, not a per-request latency metric. When metrics are disabled, the router creates no histogram and does not read the clock.
+
+For example, you can inspect the p99 router processing time in seconds:
+
+```promql
+histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(sglang:detokenizer_router_processing_seconds_bucket[5m])))
+```
+
 ## Language model metrics
 
 `sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds` measures the time from request creation in the API server to the first token. For streaming requests it ends when the first output arrives after detokenization, which may contain no printable text. Non-streaming clients only see the final response, so for them it ends when the scheduler produced the first token.
